subject: Environment
topic: Biosphere reserves of India — mixed tiers

questions.stem: The first biosphere reserve declared in India (1986) was:
questions.explanation: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve, declared on 1 September 1986, is India's first and largest. It spans Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Karnataka and includes parks like Mudumalai, Bandipur, Mukurthi, Silent Valley and Wayanad. Nanda Devi (Uttarakhand) followed in 1988; Sundarbans (WB) in 1989; Gulf of Mannar (TN) in 1989. India currently has 18 notified biosphere reserves.

questions.stem: The 'Man and the Biosphere' (MAB) programme, which recognises biosphere reserves worldwide, is run by:
questions.explanation: The Man and the Biosphere (MAB) programme was launched by UNESCO in 1971 to promote sustainable links between people and ecosystems. Of India's 18 biosphere reserves, 12 are currently part of UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves. UNEP runs environmental programmes (ozone, climate); IUCN produces the Red List of threatened species; WWF is an NGO famous for the panda logo.

questions.stem: Match the biosphere reserve with its state(s). A. Sundarbans. B. Gulf of Mannar. C. Pachmarhi. D. Dibru-Saikhowa. List-II: 1. West Bengal, 2. Tamil Nadu, 3. Madhya Pradesh, 4. Assam.
questions.explanation: Sundarbans — West Bengal (world's largest mangrove delta). Gulf of Mannar — Tamil Nadu (pearl banks, dugongs). Pachmarhi — Madhya Pradesh (Satpura range). Dibru-Saikhowa — Assam (Brahmaputra floodplain, feral horses, wetland birds).

questions.stem: The Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve of India is located in:
questions.explanation: Cold Desert Biosphere Reserve — declared 2009 — lies in the Lahaul-Spiti area of Himachal Pradesh. Home to the snow leopard, Himalayan wolf, blue sheep and ibex. Ladakh, though a cold desert in geography terms, has the Changthang Wildlife Sanctuary, not a separate biosphere reserve. Nanda Devi is Uttarakhand's; Khangchendzonga is Sikkim's.

questions.stem: A biosphere reserve is typically organised into three zones. The innermost, strictly protected area is called the:
questions.explanation: Core zone — legally protected, minimal human interference, covers the most pristine habitat. Buffer zone — surrounds the core; restricted research, traditional use and eco-tourism allowed. Transition zone (or 'area of cooperation') — outermost; human settlements and sustainable agriculture co-exist with the reserve. The three-zone concept is from the UNESCO MAB Statutory Framework.

questions.stem: The Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve is home to a famous indigenous tribe called the:
questions.explanation: Great Nicobar — the southernmost island of India and a biosphere reserve since 1989 — is home to the Shompen and Nicobarese indigenous peoples (both 'Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups'). Todas are a pastoral tribe of the Nilgiri Hills; Bhils are spread across MP/Rajasthan/Gujarat; Gonds are the largest tribal group in central India (MP, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra).

questions.stem: Panna Biosphere Reserve — famous for its diamond mines and tiger reserve — lies in which state?
questions.explanation: Panna is in the Bundelkhand region of Madhya Pradesh — best known for its Panna Tiger Reserve (tigers reintroduced successfully after 2009 when the population had dropped to zero) and for being one of India's very few diamond-mining areas. Pachmarhi and Kanha are also MP biosphere reserves / tiger reserves. Rajasthan's famous tiger reserves are Ranthambore and Sariska.
